items.text: Icarus

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: Phew! They're gone.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your father's materials proved useful.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It will not take long to finish these repairs and make some adjustments. We will still be able to perform another test flight tomorrow.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: So, it's not all bad news. Still, I have something to tell you.
She stops, hesitating to continue.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: I'm leaving Lisbon.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I see. And your flying machine?

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: Leave it be. I'll take it and our drafts to the New World and continue the project there.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: So, you have no further need of me, then?

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: That's not what I meant.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: If that means the project can be completed without further distraction, then I suppose I should welcome it. Congratulations, Jimena.
The mechanical woman stops her work abruptly and turns to her would-be test pilot.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: I've made a deal to secure my way out of here. I'm going to the beach; there'll be a boat waiting for me there.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And you will be going to the New World? That would be unwise.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You have access to many more resources here in Europe. To start over in New England would cause unnecessary delays.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: And you'd have me stay in Lisbon? Where I could be arrested at any time?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: So, you will leave? Even if that puts the project in jeopardy?
The mechanical woman's words sound like an accusation.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: I'll take all the materials with me, and our drafts. A delay, maybe, maybe a long one, but nothing I can't handle. I'll be fine.
Her confidence fades.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: Besides, this is my father's legacy, MY FATHER'S, not yours. You're only here because of him. This is my decision to make, it's my dream—our dream ...
The words taste like a lie.
She's scared.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your father built you a dream. Just like Mr. Watt's done for me.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: He wanted me to leave the laboratory to meet more people, to listen to them, and understand their ideas, their imaginations.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: He believed in the power of human cooperation. That an idea could be passed from hand to hand, like a torch or an ember, across generations.
She points at the core of her body, that very idea had come to life in her.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Thanks in part to our cooperation, our project has already come so far from where it started.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: That's true. But things have changed. If there were some glimmers of success, something I could hold on to, maybe, but ...

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: What's the difference between six seconds and nine?
Lucy packs the wings wordlessly and walks to the door.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: Lucy ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The wind is nearing optimal conditions. We should seize this final opportunity to test our work before you go.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: With our current technology, wind alone will not provide sufficient force to lift a human in a sustained or directed flight.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But a controlled glide may be possible, with the right materials.
Despite knowing that they will soon part, the only thing they can speak about is their project.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: Like a windmill? Or a water wheel? Will it use steam, like your power source?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Perhaps. A steam engine would generate a great deal of force, but it would be far too heavy to be feasible.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There is one more option: arcanum.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: You mean arcane skill? No, absolutely not!
She goes pale, as if the idea had conjured some long-forgotten nightmare.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I know. Arcanum could not be a long-term solution.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It would be impractical to have an arcanist stand by for every flight, after all.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: I don't think you really understand what other arcanists go through in this world.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: What do you mean?

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: As you no doubt heard from those soldiers, my family were smugglers. Or, really, all we did was predict the direction of the wind and sea conditions, for fishermen, sailors, and for smugglers, too.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: My father was guiding a ship out. He went with them this time, I guess, to buy some fancy new materials. But something went wrong. There was a storm. The survivors called him a "Jonah." They decided it was his fault.
Her face falls, looking stuck somewhere between anger and grief.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your father did not control the weather; he only predicted it. He should not have been blamed. That was ignorance, superstition.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Like sailors that refuse to look back as they leave port. Their motions have no true impact on the safety of the ship. It is only a mistaken belief.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: You don't understand, Lucy. They do it because looking back means that you are not ready to leave. And the sea is quick to punish those that cannot face it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The sea does not punish. It has neither feelings nor intelligence. It cannot know, nor would it care, what the sailors do.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Superstition is only a false comfort.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: But a comfort they'll still value against the vast and unpredictable sea. We can't help ourselves, humans and arcanists alike.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But it has no value at all. How much effort and time is wasted on these useless ceremonies? It could be more efficiently used for securing ropes or advancing marine technology!

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: A sailor can't do his job properly if he's thinking of home. If nothing else, people gain courage from their beliefs.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: They would be able to feel more courageous if they focused on gaining experience, and properly utilizing technology. Everything else is simply mechanistic fate. Luck, not belief.
Random luck at that. It couldn't be controlled, only computed.
But as luck would have it, at that moment, lights spring up from the other side of the beach, carried by soldiers moving swiftly toward them.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: There, on the beach!

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: No! No, the boat is late.
She realizes as she says it: it isn't late; it was already gone, along with any other boat that has a chance of getting through the tightening blockade.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: Where are they?
The panicked arcanist scans her eyes across the sea, picking out distant shadows of sails speckled against the horizon.
They must be a mile out from her and gaining distance fast.
And behind her, marching boots thud over the sand, gaining ground just as quickly.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: There is still something we can do.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Let me see the machine.
True scientific achievement will have to wait, but this will provide a temporary solution.
The light of arcane skill flashes as Lucy's piston starts to churn. She pours out a blast of steam, causing the wings to stiffen and change into an iron-gray metal.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: Wh-what is this? You never told me you could do anything like this!

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: What did you do to it?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: This may be strong enough to keep you in the air, but I cannot make any guarantees.
Jimena dons the now metallic wings, flapping them like a fledgling eager to take off.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Control your altitude, and aim as best as you can for the nearest boat.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You must lie flat and keep your body parallel to the water.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: What if I fall?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Then they may catch you, but you will be caught if you stay here.
Lucy is right. There is only one way out, and she must take it. Nervous feet find their pace. She runs toward the sea.
Extending her wings, she leaps with all her strength up and over the water.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Arms open, body flat, and stay balanced.

items.speaker: Jimena
items.text: Lucy!
The wind lifts her up surely and steadily.
Jimena's stomach churns as she makes for the horizon, chasing toward the bare outlines of masts against the setting sun.
From the beach, there is no more sign of the little pilot. No way to know whether she landed safely. Against all odds, the mechanical woman finds herself hoping her friend did not look back.
A seabird skims over her from the darkness of the sea toward the lights approaching from the beach.
Jimena's flight is a little unsteady at first, but she flies. No one can take that from her now.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: She has flown the coop, gentlemen.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: And you just let her go?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am under no obligation to catch her. Besides, how could I?

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Ay! Find her! Swim if you've got to! Vamos!
The soldiers pay the woman no mind as they rush up the ridge to get a better view, nor does she mind them. Her little bird is long past where they could reach her.
Though arcane skill was not how either of them had envisioned achieving it.
The mechanical woman heads back toward the city walls, lost in thought, scarcely noticing the blaring horns ringing out across the port.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We have tried so many designs.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: A variety of materials, shapes, structures, countless formula adjustments, and yet only arcane skill proved sufficient—a shortcut—one wholly unreliable in any practical application.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: They had made so much progress, only to part without a solution.
Jimena. That frightened little bird—she could not blame her, though she wanted to. All this so she could escape and leave her with nothing, not even a working theory.
Crackling shots ring out from the beach, the soldiers firing vainly into the sky as their captain rages. But Jimena is well beyond sight now, and the reach of their shot.
As if to bring her back to her senses, a tiny crab crawls out of the sand and snaps at her feet.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hmm? You want me to step aside, am I right?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your chitin is certainly harder than most things, but no match for metal. An arthropod of your size simply does not have the size or strength to damage me.
She catches the crab gently, scanning it for a moment before allowing it to scurry away into the sea.
It disappears beneath the waves, just as her friend did in the evening sky.
Never to come back.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I let you cheat. But to find a real workable solution, there will be a price to pay.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It will take time, determination, and courage.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And now you chose to give up, Jimena.
